newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market pre-holiday calm - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market pre-holiday calm - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets on Thursday were quiet before the Independence Day holiday on Friday, feedlot sources said.
Major cattle slaughter and beef processing plants will be closed on Friday, but operating normal weekend hours on Saturday and full hours on Monday, company officials and market sources said.

Packers reportedly were comfortably supplied with live inventory for early next week following active sales this week at $63.00 per cwt, sources said. Bids Thursday at $62.00 were passed by owners asking $63.00 for remaining cattle.

Outlooks for next week's fed cattle prices were steady to weak amid projections for a seasonal drop in beef demand after this weekend's holiday-related cookouts and forecasts for increased numbers of cattle coming to market the rest of July, feedlot sources said.
Cattle sales this week kept most feedlots fairly current, but some cattle were still expected to be carried over to next week's showlists, they said.
Direct fed cattle sales for the week through Thursday morning in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area were tabbed by USDA at 78,700 head.
Kansas sales through early Thursday afternoon were pegged at 76,600 head.
